uttara-gonobhaban.desc: Built by the Dighapatia rajas in the 18th century and rebuilt after the 1897 earthquake, the palace stands inside a moated compound with a clock-tower gate. Lawns and old trees surround the main building, including rare imported plants and statues in the gardens. It became the official northern residence of the head of government after independence, which is why it is called Uttara Gonobhaban. Visitors can walk the grounds and see the museum when open.
blocks: How to get there
About 3 km north of Natore town centre at Dighapatia; take a rickshaw or auto-rickshaw.
Good to know
Access can be restricted during official use, so check before going.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
laxmipur-aushodhi-gram.desc: In the Laxmipur-Kholabaria area of Natore Sadar, many farming families have turned to growing medicinal plants instead of ordinary crops. Fields of aloe vera, shatamuli, basak and other herbs supply herbal medicine makers across the country. The practice began with a few local pioneers and spread through the villages. Walking the field paths, you can talk with growers about how each plant is used.
blocks: How to get there
Hire an auto-rickshaw from Natore town to Laxmipur-Kholabaria union.
Good to know
Ask before entering fields or photographing workers.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
chalan-beel.desc: Chalan Beel spreads across parts of Natore, Pabna and Sirajganj, a low basin fed by several rivers. In the rainy season the beel swells into a vast sheet of water dotted with villages on raised mounds, and boats become the main transport. As the water drops, fishermen work the channels and the land turns to rice and mustard. Winter brings migratory birds, and sunsets over the open water are unforgettable.
blocks: How to get there
From Natore, go to Singra or Gurudaspur by bus or CNG and hire a boat locally; the Natore–Bogura and Bonpara–Hatikumrul roads also cross the beel.
Good to know
Take a boat in the late afternoon in monsoon. Use a life jacket where available and avoid storms.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
chalan-beel-museum.desc: The Chalan Beel Museum began in 1978 in a room of Khubjipur High School, started by Professor M.A. Hamid to save the history of the Chalan Beel region, and came under the Department of Archaeology in 1989. Its collection includes old hand-written Qurans on tulot paper, deeds said to be in Rani Bhabani's hand, stone images of Surya and Vishnu, and coins from about ninety countries. The museum has been badly neglected and some items were moved to Mahasthan, but it remains a rare look at the beel country's past.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Natore to Gurudaspur, then an auto-rickshaw to Khubjipur village.
Good to know
Opening hours are irregular, so ask locally before you go. Pair it with a boat trip on Chalan Beel in the monsoon.

glance: Markets and local restaurants in Singra and Gurudaspur
chalan-beel-fish.desc: Chalan Beel has long been a source of freshwater fish for North Bengal. As the monsoon water recedes, nets and traps bring in koi, shing, magur, puti and many small species. Local cooks prepare them with onion, garlic and green chilli, or in light jhol with vegetables. Some of the catch is also sun-dried into shutki along the beel's edges.
blocks: Good to know
Ask for whatever was caught that morning.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
natore-rajbari.desc: The Natore Raj family became one of the largest zamindari estates in Bengal in the 18th century. Its best-known ruler, Rani Bhabani, is remembered for her charity, temples and public works across the region. The large compound holds several palace buildings, temples and ponds, set among tall trees and wide lawns. It is now a public park, popular with families on weekends.
blocks: How to get there
In Natore town; any rickshaw will take you to the Rajbari.
Good to know
Weekday mornings are quieter. Some buildings are fragile, so respect barriers.

glance: Long-established sweet shops in central Natore town, especially around Lalbazar
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
natore-kacha-golla.desc: Despite its name, kacha golla is not a golla (ball). It is fresh chhana kneaded and cooked briefly with sugar, often with a hint of cardamom, leaving it soft, moist and only lightly sweet. Natore's version has been praised for generations and is the sweet everyone buys on a visit. It must be eaten fresh, which makes having it in Natore itself special.
blocks: Good to know
It does not keep long; eat within a day or two, or keep it cool.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
bonpara-lourdes-church.desc: The Catholic mission at Bonpara in Baraigram upazila dates from 1940, when Christian families from Kaliganj in Gazipur settled here. In 2010 a new, richly decorated church was built beside the old one, along with a very large statue of Mary, the mother of Jesus. Visitors of all faiths stop to see it, and Christian pilgrims come from far away. The parish also runs schools and a college.
blocks: How to get there
Bonpara is on the Natore–Dhaka highway; any bus stops at Bonpara, and the church is right by the road.
Good to know
Dress modestly and stay quiet during Mass. Christmas is the busiest and most festive time.

glance: Village markets and roadside sellers in Lalpur and Baraigram upazilas in winter
lalpur-khejur-gur.desc: Natore has more than six lakh date palms, and each winter gachhis tap them for sap for about two and a half months. The sap is boiled down in wide pans into solid patali or runny jhola gur. Lalpur upazila alone makes far more than any other part of the district, followed by Baraigram and Gurudaspur. Locals eat jhola gur with muri or fresh pitha, and patali travels well as a gift.
blocks: Good to know
Ask to see it being boiled at a gachhi's yard; adulterated gur is a known problem, so buy from the maker if you can.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
shahid-sagar-natore.desc: On 5 May 1971 Pakistani troops, helped by local collaborators, stormed the North Bengal Sugar Mill at Gopalpur in Lalpur. They lined up more than a hundred workers and officers beside the mill's Gopal Sagar pond and shot them; only a few survived. The pond, said to have stayed red for years, is now called Shahid Sagar. A memorial was unveiled in 1973 and a small museum opened in 2000, and bullet marks on the steps are painted red. Every 5 May the mill and the town mark the day.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or train to Gopalpur (Lalpur) from Natore or Ishwardi; the memorial is inside the sugar mill area.
Good to know
This is a place of mourning: keep it quiet and respectful. Check that the museum is open if you want to go inside.

glance: 200 km to Natore by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
halti-beel.desc: Halti Beel lies west of Natore town in Naldanga upazila. In the monsoon the beel fills up and a narrow road through it sits just above or even below the water, creating the feeling of driving across a lake. Local boats take visitors out to small islands of villages and trees. In the dry months the water retreats and rice fields take over.
blocks: How to get there
Take a CNG or bus from Natore towards Naldanga, then a local auto-rickshaw to the beel road.
Good to know
Go on a weekday to avoid crowds. Do not wade on the submerged road; currents can be strong.
